taxonomic_note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO and Flora of North America. Poinsettia dentata is retained as a synonym. This species belongs to the difficult E. dentata group and should be compared directly with E. davidii.
look_here_first: LOOK AT THE LEAF UNDERSIDE, THEN COLLECT THE MATURE SEED IF YOU NEED TO SEPARATE THIS FROM E. davidii. Both are upright annual spurges with coarsely toothed opposite (sometimes upper alternate) leaves, inconspicuous green CYATHIA, and developing three-lobed capsules. E. dentata tends toward LONG, SOFT THREADLIKE hairs beneath the leaves, smaller capsules (3.5–4 mm wide), and smaller SEEDS ROUNDED IN CROSS SECTION with an even cover of minute bumps. E. davidii tends to have SHORT, STIFF, TAPERED hairs, larger capsules (4–4.8 mm), and ANGULAR more irregularly tuberculate seeds. Color, leaf teeth, reddish spots or branch habit alone DO NOT confirm this species. If neither hairs nor seeds are clear, label E. dentata–davidii group or Euphorbia sp.

project_inclusion.range_basis: BONAP/NPSOT-backed county distribution locks Hays, Bexar, and Burnet; additional target-zone records occur in Edwards, Gillespie, Kerr, Kimble, Llano, Real, Schleicher, Sutton, Travis, and Uvalde.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: County PASS is based on explicit county distribution evidence, not statewide native status alone.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbia sect. Poinsettia: annual with milky latex and cyathia; in the dentata group, leaf-hair texture, capsule size, and especially mature seed morphology carry the identification.
morphology_keys.growth_form: Annual taprooted herb; stems erect or ascending, usually about 15–60 cm.
morphology_keys.leaves: Usually opposite; blades about 30–70 × 4–35 mm, narrowly lanceolate to suborbiculate, often broadest below the middle, with coarse crenate-dentate to doubly crenate margins.
morphology_keys.hairs: Abaxial leaf surface long-pilose with weak, filiform hairs; adaxial surface sparsely pilose to nearly glabrous. This softer/longer hair texture is useful against E. davidii.
morphology_keys.cyathium: Usually (1–)2 green glands, sessile and broadly attached; openings oblong; appendages absent.
morphology_keys.fruit: Capsules depressed-globose, about 2.5–2.8 × 3.5–4 mm, 3-lobed and glabrous.
morphology_keys.seed: Seeds pale gray to black, ovoid and rounded in cross section, about 2.1–2.7 × 1.7–2.1 mm, with evenly distributed minute tubercles; caruncle about 0.4–0.6 mm.
best_field_traits: Annual usually 15–60 cm, upright to ascending branched taprooted herb (supporting habit only).
Leaves typically OPPOSITE on many nodes; sometimes upper leaves alternate; blades variable, often 30–70 mm long.
Broad coarse crenate-dentate to double-crenate leaf edges, not a species-only trait.
Upper reproductive nodes can have several tiny green cyathia and developing green THREE-LOBED CAPSULES.
Under mature leaf: long WEAK, THREADLIKE hairs (abaxial) in E. dentata; compare shorter stiff strongly tapered hairs in E. davidii.
Mature capsule typically glabrous, about 2.5–2.8 mm tall and 3.5–4 mm WIDE. Measure actual width, don't guess from screen size.
Mature seed about 2.1–2.7 × 1.7–2.1 mm; OVOID ROUNDED cross section, finely and evenly covered with minute bumps (best tie-breaker).
Poinsettia dentata is a synonym, not a distinct native taxon or horticultural selection.
morphology_keys.comparison_training: E. dentata = softer/longer abaxial hairs + smaller capsule + smaller rounded, evenly pebbled seed. E. davidii = shorter stiffer hairs, often pustule-based + larger capsule + larger angular, irregularly tuberculate seed.
morphology_keys.family_genus: Euphorbiaceae; Euphorbia sect. Poinsettia. A cyathium is a tiny cup containing one reduced female flower and numerous separate reduced male flowers; green cup-like glands are NOT petals. Fruit is a three-lobed dry capsule with seeds inside.
field_id_steps: 1. Full plant side photo: upright annual with several branched terminal reproductive heads.
2. Leaf arrangement at one mature node: photograph both opposite petioles, toothed margins, and any alternate upper leaves.
3. Turn a fully mature undamaged leaf over (do NOT rely on upper-surface hairs). Macro the LOWER surface with a 1 mm reference.
4. Locate the tiny cyathia and 3-lobed capsules; label them correctly rather than calling green fruit a flower.
5. Photograph a fully mature intact capsule at 1 mm scale, then photograph the released seed from TWO sides under 10–20× magnification.
6. Confirm ROUNDED seed cross section and EVENLY minute-tuberculate surface before separating E. dentata from E. davidii.
7. When only coarsely toothed leaves and green capsules are photographed, retain E. dentata–davidii GROUP, not a confident species ID.
what_not_to_trust: flower/cyathium without underside hairs and mature seed
morphology_keys.ecology_and_management: Native within the project's Hays target range and occurs on disturbed open ground, prairies, road margins and streamside openings. Disturbance is not proof the plant is introduced; avoid pulling by default when restoration objectives include local annual-forb diversity. Latex can irritate eyes/skin: use gloves and avoid intentionally rupturing plants to train workers.
morphology_keys.crew_field_script: See those opposite toothed leaves and green little three-lobed fruits? You've got a toothed-spurge GROUP. Flip one mature leaf over and look at hairs under a loupe. Long floppy threads point to dentata; short stiff tapering hairs to davidii. For a confident answer, check a 2–3 mm ripe seed: rounded/evenly pebbled versus angular/irregular bumps. No seed or hair? Euphorbia dentata–davidii group is a perfectly good field call.

comparisons.key_distinctions: E. davidii is the primary look-alike. Distinguish by abaxial leaf hair type and seed sculpture/cross section, not leaf silhouette or color. E. cyathophora and E. heterophylla may resemble upright toothed spurges but their distinctive distal bracts and gland configuration belong to different morphological groupings.

items.label: Look closer: coarsely toothed leaves
items.image_role: Simple leaves showing unequal broad marginal teeth and opposite/near-opposite upper-node context
items.creator: Max Licher / swbiodiversity.org
items.caption: The green mid-stem leaf has obvious broad teeth along its outer edge; nearby leaves and tiny floral structures cluster at the upper node. Leaf teeth support E. dentata-group recognition but cannot separate E. dentata from E. davidii.
items.why_it_matters: A crew member can identify the right plant GROUP from foliage, then knows to turn a leaf over for hairs rather than deciding prematurely.

items.label: Confirm the Euphorbia-style three-lobed capsule
items.image_role: Green developing three-lobed capsules clustered among leaves and inconspicuous reproductive cups
items.creator: Max Licher / swbiodiversity.org
items.caption: The rounded green structures surrounding the central branching point are separate three-lobed developing CAPSULES—not berries, not one five-petaled flower, and not seeds. Fine seed-coat sculpture is not visible.
items.why_it_matters: A three-lobed capsule plus tiny cyathia supports Euphorbia. Mature seed characters and underside-leaf hairs are still needed to confirm against E. davidii.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Toothed spurge: STOP at the dentata/davidii pair until you see hair or seed
steps: Find branching annual stems with opposite toothed leaves and terminal small reproductive clusters.
Identify the actual green THREE-LOBED CAPSULE and tiny cyathium structures. No showy petals.
Turn a mature leaf over and photograph the hair type: long soft threads should favor dentata.
A mature seed is the best tie-breaker: rounded with fine even bumps favors dentata, angular unevenly lumpy favors davidii.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: No underside leaf macro + no fully ripe seed = Euphorbia dentata/davidii GROUP, not a species-level certainty.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: None of these public photos shows a decisive mature seed or abaxial hair base. The arrow-labeled green capsules are developing fruits and look similar in both species.
